pieces.title: The pieces
pieces.intro: Each piece moves its own way. Take the piece to every star: your opponent does not move.

towers.title: Towers
towers.intro: A piece can climb onto another (ツケ) instead of going to an empty square. The taller the tower, the farther its top piece reaches.

hand.title: Pieces in hand
hand.intro: Pieces in hand (新) enter the board instead of a move, on an empty square or on top of one of your pieces.

jumpers.title: Jumping pieces
jumpers.intro: The Cannon, Musketeer and Archer jump forward over towers as tall as they are, or shorter.

betrayal.title: Betrayal
betrayal.intro: When the Tactician climbs onto a tower with enemy pieces, you may swap them for the same pieces from your hand (寝返り).

marshal.title: Marshal in danger
marshal.intro: If your Marshal is captured, you lose. While it is attacked, only the moves that save it are offered.

mate.title: Mate
mate.intro: A player with no safe move left loses: that is mate. Now the computer defends as well as it can.

draft.title: The draft
draft.intro: In the Intermediate and Advanced modes, each player sets up their position by placing one piece at a time in their territory (初期配置).

pieces-marshal.instruction: The Marshal moves one square in any direction. Go through every star.
pieces-marshal.hint: It can go to any of the eight squares around it.

pieces-general.instruction: The General moves any number of squares in a straight line and one square diagonally.
pieces-general.hint: Go up the whole file in a single move.

pieces-lieutenant.instruction: The Lieutenant General moves any number of squares diagonally and one square in a straight line.
pieces-lieutenant.hint: Start with the long diagonal to the edge.

pieces-major.instruction: The Major General moves one square forward, sideways, backward and on the forward diagonals.
pieces-major.hint: It does not go back diagonally.

pieces-samurai.instruction: The Samurai moves one square forward, on the forward diagonals and backward.

pieces-lancer.instruction: The Lancer moves up to two squares forward, one on the forward diagonals and one backward.
pieces-lancer.hint: Two squares forward count as a single move.

pieces-knight.instruction: The Knight moves up to two squares forward or backward and one sideways.
pieces-knight.hint: Sideways it goes only one square per move.

pieces-ninja.instruction: The Ninja moves up to two squares along any diagonal.
pieces-ninja.hint: It can also stop on the first square of the diagonal.

pieces-fortress.instruction: The Fortress moves one square forward, sideways and on the backward diagonals.
pieces-fortress.hint: To go back, use the backward diagonals.

pieces-soldier.instruction: The Soldier moves one square forward or backward. Capture the enemy Soldier by moving onto its square.
pieces-soldier.hint: On the enemy square, choose to capture.

pieces-tactician.instruction: The Tactician moves one square on the forward diagonals and one backward.
pieces-tactician.hint: Combine the diagonals with the step back.

towers-stack.instruction: Stack the Samurai on top of your Soldier.
towers-stack.hint: Move the Samurai to the Soldier and choose to stack.

towers-reach.instruction: At tier 2, every direction reaches one square farther. Reach the star in a single move.
towers-reach.hint: On top of the tower, the Samurai goes up to two squares forward.

towers-reach-three.instruction: At tier 3 it reaches two squares farther. Reach the star in a single move.
towers-reach-three.hint: On top of a tower of 3, the Samurai goes up to three squares forward.

towers-taller.instruction: You can only capture a tower as tall as your piece, or shorter. Climb a tier and capture the tower of 2.
towers-taller.hint: First stack the Samurai on the Soldier in front of it.

hand-drop.instruction: Place the Soldier from your hand on the star.
hand-drop.hint: Pick the piece in your hand, below the board, then the square.

hand-zone.instruction: You can only place pieces up to the rank of your most advanced piece. Take the Lancer to the star.
hand-zone.hint: Place the Lancer on an allowed rank, then move it up.

hand-stack.instruction: You can also place a piece on top of one of yours. Place the Samurai on the star.
hand-stack.hint: The star is on top of your Soldier.

hand-attack.instruction: Capture the enemy Soldier with the Samurai from your hand.
hand-attack.hint: Place the Samurai where it reaches the Soldier on the next move.

jumpers-cannon.instruction: The Cannon jumps to the third square ahead, over whatever is in the way.
jumpers-cannon.hint: Pieces as tall as it do not block the jump.

jumpers-musketeer.instruction: The Musketeer jumps to the second square ahead and moves one square on the backward diagonals.
jumpers-musketeer.hint: After the jump, come back diagonally.

jumpers-archer.instruction: The Archer jumps two squares forward, straight or to the side. Go through both stars.
jumpers-archer.hint: The first jump goes to the side.

jumpers-tall.instruction: A tower taller than the piece blocks the jump. Raise the Cannon a tier and jump to the star.
jumpers-tall.hint: Stack the Cannon on the Soldier next to it.

betrayal-move.instruction: Climb the Tactician onto the enemy Soldier and choose to betray: it becomes yours.
betrayal-move.hint: You have a Soldier in hand for the swap.

betrayal-drop.instruction: Betrayal also works when you place the Tactician from your hand on a tower of yours with an enemy below.
betrayal-drop.hint: Place the Tactician on top of your Soldier.

betrayal-tower.instruction: To betray, you need a matching piece in hand for each enemy in the tower. Betray the whole tower.
betrayal-tower.hint: The Tactician is already at tier 2, tall enough to climb the tower.

marshal-escape.instruction: The enemy General attacks your Marshal. Get your Marshal out of the attack.

marshal-capture.instruction: Capture the piece that attacks your Marshal.

marshal-block.instruction: Block the attack by placing the Fortress from your hand on the star.
marshal-block.hint: A piece in the way cuts the General’s attack.

mate-general.hint: The Lieutenant General already covers the diagonals: attack along the rank.

mate-archer.hint: Take the General to the last rank.

mate-corner.hint: The Marshal is in the corner: attack along its file.

mate-two-cannon.hint: Start with a check by the Lancer.

mate-two-archer.hint: Start with a check by the General.

draft-marshal.instruction: The first piece of the draft is always the Marshal. Place it in your territory, the first three ranks.
draft-marshal.hint: Pick the Marshal in your hand.

draft-place.instruction: Place pieces from your hand on both stars.
draft-place.hint: Any piece will do, inside your territory.

draft-done.instruction: When you do not want to place more pieces, declare done. As you play second, the draft ends right away.

learn.title: How to play Gungi
learn.lead: Gungi (軍儀) is the board game from HUNTER×HUNTER. We use the official rules published by Universal Music (2022). The full specification, with sources and interpretations, is in the project repository.
learn.objective: Capture the opposing Marshal (帥). In practice the game ends in mate: when the player to move has no move that keeps their own Marshal safe, they lose, even if the Marshal is not under attack at that moment. A game also ends by resignation, time, the same position repeated 4 times (draw) or agreement.
learn.board: 9×9 board, 25 pieces per player. The three rows closest to you are your starting territory. Captured pieces leave the game for good.
learn.towers:
Instead of capturing, you can stack your piece on top of another one, yours or your opponent’s. Towers hold up to 3 pieces (2 in the simpler modes).
Only the top piece moves, and its tier (the tower height) extends its reach in the directions it already moves: +1 square at tier 2, +2 at tier 3 (directions that already reach the edge stay as they are).
To capture or stack, your piece must be on a tier equal to or higher than the height of the target tower.
When you capture a tower, all of its enemy pieces leave the game; yours stay, with the capturing piece on top.
Nothing can be stacked on the Marshal.
learn.hand: Pieces you did not place during the draft stay in your hand. On your turn, instead of moving, you can drop one of them on an empty square or on one of your pieces, on any row up to the row of your most advanced piece.
learn.setup: White always moves first. In the Introductory and Beginner modes the starting position is fixed. In the Intermediate and Advanced modes the players take turns placing pieces in their own territory, starting with the Marshal. A player who does not want to place more pieces declares 済み (done). If the first player declares, the second may keep going; when the second declares, the draft ends for both. In casual games, whoever creates the game can choose the free draft option, where each player places pieces until declaring done and the draft only ends when both are done.
learn.piecesHint: Pick a piece to see how far it reaches at each tower level and to practise on the board.

notes.marshal: If you have no safe move, you lose. Nothing can be stacked on it.
notes.general: Unlimited straight lines, unaffected by the tier.
notes.lieutenant: Unlimited diagonals, unaffected by the tier.
notes.cannon: Jumps forward over towers of equal or lower height.
notes.archer: Shoots straight ahead and along the forward diagonals, over towers of equal or lower height.
notes.musketeer: Jumps forward over towers of equal or lower height.
notes.tactician: Can betray: when stacking on enemy pieces, it swaps all of them for matching pieces from your hand.

blind.settingHelp: In games, the board gets a text version: every move is announced, and a field takes typed moves and questions about the position. The board stays on screen for anyone helping.
blind.title: Game as text
blind.commandHelp: Type h and Enter to hear the help.
blind.help:
To play, type the destination square and the piece, for example 4-7 samurai, or the from and to squares, for example 4-8 4-7. To drop a piece from the hand, type the piece and the square, for example ninja 4-7. The machine notation and the rulebook notation work too.
To say the action, add capture, stack or betray. To pick the tier, type it with the square, for example 4-7-2.
Commands: p, the whole position. c and a square, for example c 4-7, the tower on that square. m, the hands. l and a square, the moves of the piece on that square. u, the last move. r, the clocks. done, to finish the draft. draw and resign, in online games.
When a move can be played more than one way, the site lists numbered options: type the number.
To step through the moves: < goes back one, > forward one, start and end. g reads the goal, when the page has one.
Right below there is a keyboard board: arrow keys to move between the squares, Enter to pick the piece and then the destination, Escape to cancel.
blind.studyHelp: In this study, every move is read with its comment and drawings. d reads the drawings again. The author draws with arrow 5-7 5-5 red and paint 4-5 blue (the same command erases), and clear erases the drawings of the move.
blind.editorHelp: In the editor: 4-7 white samurai puts the piece on top of the square, remove 4-7 takes the top piece off, hand black samurai puts a piece in Black's hand and remove hand black samurai takes it out. clear empties the board, turn white picks who moves and p reads the position.
